newsitem.title: FRANCE: Metaleurop eyes Nordenhan start this week.
newsitem.headline: Metaleurop eyes Nordenhan start this week.

text.p: Metaleurop SA said on Tuesday that it planned to restart lead production at its plant in Nordenham, Germany, by the end of the week.
"Production will start at the end of the week," a company spkeswoman told Reuters.
She said the heating of the the smelting furnace would start on Thursday and production on Sunday or Monday.
In early January Metaleurop announced it had halted production at Nordenham at end 1996 until the last week of January.
The shutdown was for technical adjusments and repairs.
Metaleurop, a unit of PREUSSAG AG, started production at the new 90,000 tonnes low cost smelter in March 1996.
It initially said output at the new plant was to be limited to 70 percent of capacity during its first twelve months of operation.
That target was later cut to 50-55 percent of capacity after Metaleurop closed the smelter in July to make technical adjustments. Production at the smelter restarted in September.
The spokeswoman said it was premature at this stage to provide a new production target for Nordenham.
She indicated that for financial year ended September 30, 1996, Metaleurop's lead production fell by 50,000 tonnes to 310,000 tonnes, mostly the result of difficulties experienced by Nordenham.
